name: Chong Qing Xiao Mian
why: A cramped, always-full Chinatown room for Chongqing-style noodles that numb without flattening the broth. Strong on the bowl, thin on story.
story: A small Kearny Street shop that sticks to regional Chinese noodles, with a handful of tight tables and a steady crowd. The dan dan noodles come in a nutty, rich broth loaded with wheat noodles and enough Sichuan pepper to leave a tingle, and wonton and spicy beef soups fill out the rest of the menu.
order: Dan dan noodles; the spicy beef noodle soup if you want a full bowl of broth.
practical: Small room, expect to share space at lunch
flags: Single editorial source (Infatuation, Dec 2023); no ownership or history found.
Hours from a search summary of listing sites; confirm.

name: Lung Fung Bakery
why: The baked BBQ pork bun here is the Richmond's most-chased pastry and sells out in batches. Everything else is a plain neighborhood bakery counter.
story: A plain Clement Street bakery known for baked BBQ pork buns with crisp tops and enough filling to spill out the sides. They often come off the sheet still warm and go fast, so locals turn up at the 7:30 opening and buy by the dozen. Ham-and-corn and green onion buns are the backup.
order: Baked BBQ pork buns, a dozen; ham-and-corn bun if they're gone.
practical: Opens 7:30 am; pork buns sell out in waves
hours: Opens 7:30 am (Infatuation); closing time not confirmed
flags: Single editorial source (Infatuation, Dec 2024).
Cash only comes from an Infatuation guide summary in search, not the review page itself.
Area set to Central Richmond (Clement at 19th/20th Ave); candidate said Outer Richmond.
Discovery note about $2 egg tarts not sourced; left out.

name: Tia Margarita
kind: Northern Mexican restaurant and bar, since 1963
why: A 1963 family restaurant that kept its neon marquee, a horseshoe bar older than itself and a menu written by its first chef. Three generations of one family have run it.
story: Opened in 1963 by two bartender couples in a bar with spare back rooms; chef Alejandro Espinosa wrote the Northern Mexican menu. Virginia Hobbs brought her daughters in after her partners died, and her granddaughter runs it now. The neon sign dates from opening day and the horseshoe bar from The Bostonian, the bar before it.
order: A fresh lime margarita at the horseshoe bar, then carne asada or chile rellenos.
practical: Stayed open through a 1988 fire and the 1989 quake
flags: History is from the restaurant's own About page; Hoodline (Apr 2023) says the recipes are unchanged since 1963 (search summary, not fetched).
SFGate also profiled it (2023) but disallows fetching; not used.
Area set to Central Richmond (19th Ave at Clement).
Hours not confirmed.

name: Thai Nghiep Ky Mi Gia
why: A booth-lined noodle house where the duck leg egg noodle soup draws a midday crowd for about $15. Little is published about who runs it.
story: Noodle soups make up most of the menu at this Noriega Street room with red leather booths. The one to cross the Avenues for is egg noodles with wontons and a braised duck leg whose bone slides right out, in a clear, savory broth. It fills up at lunch.
order: Egg noodle soup with wontons and braised duck leg.
flags: Infatuation review (May 2024) is the only editorial source; Hungry Onion thread not fetched.
Free soy milk and dry-style #13 came from earlier search summaries; left out until confirmed.
Area set to Central Sunset (Noriega at 21st Ave); candidate said Inner Sunset.
Hours not confirmed; morning hours unverified, so only midday is listed.

name: Kingdom of Dumpling
why: The best-known stop on Taraval's run of dumpling houses, a small family room built around a long list of boiled and pan-fried dumplings. Plain inside; you come for the plates.
story: Owner David Li ran this small Taraval room as David's Kitchen before renaming it Kingdom of Dumpling by 2008 to put the family specialty up front. The menu runs to well over a dozen fillings, from pork with corn to lamb with Chinese greens, plus soup dumplings and potstickers.
order: Steamed pork and corn dumplings and a plate of potstickers.
hours: Mon to Thu and Sun 11 am to 9:30 pm; Fri and Sat to 10 pm (own site)
flags: Food GPS review is from July 2008; menu details may have changed.
SFGate covers Taraval's dumpling cluster and a 2007 opening, but disallows fetching; not used.
A frozen-dumpling storefront on Taraval near 30th Ave run by the same owner appears in search summaries only; left out.

name: Giuliana's Just For You Cafe
why: A homey Dogpatch diner famous for house-made beignets and bread, and said to have inspired the restaurant in Bob's Burgers. It closed in 2023 and reopened under a new owner.
story: Started in 1990 and a Dogpatch fixture after moving down from Potrero Hill, Just for You was known for house-baked bread, chicken and waffles and big New Orleans-style beignets. It closed abruptly in April 2023. Michael Tufo, who owns an Excelsior Italian deli, reopened it that summer, renamed for his daughter, keeping the beignets and the diner feel.
order: Beignets for the table, then a scramble or the house breakfast plate.
flags: Changed hands in 2023; the old owner's 33-year run is the story, so the new room needs a visit to judge.
Confirm it is still open in 2026: the newest evidence is aggregator listings.
The 2002 move to Dogpatch comes from a Chronicle search summary (not fetchable).
justforyoucafe.com is the pre-2023 site with old hours; not used for hours.

name: Goat Hill Pizza
why: A 1975 hilltop pizzeria with a sourdough crust and an all-you-can-eat Monday where servers walk slices around the room. Families come back across generations.
story: Five friends in their twenties took over a burned-out barbecue joint on Potrero Hill in 1975 and built a neighborhood hangout on sourdough crust. The owners kept a black goat named Hilda out back into the mid-1980s; she is still on the boxes. All-you-can-eat Monday costs $19.75, a nod to the opening year.
order: Come on a Monday and take whatever comes off the trays; a sourdough-crust pie any other night.
flags: History is from the pizzeria's own About page (updated Nov 2025).
Potrero View (40th anniversary) not fetched.
Turned 50 in 2025 (Chronicle headline in search; not fetchable).

name: G & L Bakery & Restaurant
why: A cash-only Leland Avenue bakery whose pork buns come out of the oven early, across from the branch library. A neighborhood stop, not a destination.
story: A small Chinese bakery and cafe on Leland Avenue, across from the Visitacion Valley library, selling pork buns hot from the oven first thing, plus dim sum to go and plates for lunch and dinner. Neighbors time their walk for the first batch, around 7:15 in the morning.
order: Baked pork buns from the first batch, around 7:15 am.
hours: Mon to Sat 7 am to 7 pm (2020, confirm)
flags: Community/listing sources only.
Only source is a 2020 post by the neighboring Mission Blue cafe; hours may have changed.
Consider dropping unless a visit finds more to say.

name: La Méditerranée
why: A 1979 family room on Fillmore that taught the street to eat hummus and still serves meze from Armenian and Lebanese family recipes. A listed SF Legacy Business.
story: Levon Der Bedrossian opened it in 1979, when few locals knew hummus; he sent out meze platters to wary couples and told them not to pay if they disliked them, and they came back with friends. The recipes are his family's Armenian and Lebanese ones. His son Vanick has run the kitchen since 2007.
order: The meze platter, plus the Armenian potato salad.
practical: Small room near Fillmore and Sacramento
flags: Owner name spelled Lavon in New Fillmore (2009) and Levon on the restaurant site; used Levon.
A 2024-25 building sale put the lease in doubt; ConnectCRE and Chronicle headlines say it is staying. Confirm.

name: Peña's Bakery
why: The original Peña family panadería, opened in 1997 by a Guadalajara baker after nearly two decades of saving. Family members still work the counter.
story: Ramon Peña arrived from Guadalajara on July 4, 1978 with his wife and four kids, baked at La Borinqueña, and by 1997 had saved enough to open this shop at 39th and International. Ramon and his daughters became fixtures at the counter, while son Arturo runs a second Peña's on Foothill. The cases hold conchas, canastas and fruit empanadas.
order: A concha and a custard canasta; ask early about a torta, which is made off-menu in the morning.
practical: Second family shop at 34th Ave and Foothill Blvd
flags: East Bay Express article is from 2017; who works the counter now is unconfirmed.

name: La Grana Fish
why: A Sinaloa-style seafood truck with a crisp Baja fish taco and a bar next door for a michelada. Started on 50th Avenue in 2018 and has since moved to San Leandro Street.
story: The truck opened on 50th Avenue in 2018 with an odd pairing of seafood tacos and loaded baked potatoes. It now parks beside the Aloha Club in the Fruitvale, with roomy seating and a bar that sells michelada mixes. People come for the queso-birria, but the light-battered Baja fish taco with chipotle crema is the one to order.
order: Baja fish taco with chipotle crema; a ceviche tostada on the side.
practical: Parks at 3221 San Leandro St, beside the Aloha Club
Bar seating next to the truck

name: Lois the Pie Queen
why: Possibly California's oldest Black-owned restaurant, still in family hands, with walls of photos and a breakfast named for Reggie Jackson. The pies are the reason for the name.
story: Lois Davis cooked for her father's church and, with her sister, catered up to 10,000 sandwiches a day for Black shipyard workers in the 1940s. She and her husband Roland opened in Berkeley in 1951 and moved to 60th and Adeline in the mid-1970s. Her son Chris runs it. The Reggie Jackson breakfast means two pork chops and two eggs.
order: The Reggie Jackson breakfast, then a slice of pie to go.
practical: Walls lined with photos of Black American figures
flags: Resy piece is from October 2022; Chris Davis said then he planned to hand the restaurant to his son Corey. Confirm who runs it now.
Which pies are best is not covered in fetched sources; order line kept general.

name: Daol Tofu & Korean BBQ
why: A chef-owned Korean room that does far more than soft tofu, including bo ssam and a bubbling army-stew hot pot. It feels like being cooked for by an aunt.
story: Chef-owner Sunny Bae took over the old Casserole House space on Telegraph in 2017 and opened within a week of its closing. Daol, she says, means all things bring luck. The menu runs from soondubu and dolsot bibimbap to bo ssam and an army-stew casserole of kimchi, Spam and ramen, lit at the table.
order: Seafood soondubu, or the army-stew casserole for a group.
practical: Lunch and dinner with an afternoon break
hours: Tue to Sun 11 am to 2:30 pm and 5 to 9:30 pm (own site, confirm)
flags: East Bay Express review is from May 2017; confirm Sunny Bae still owns it.
Area set to Temescal (Telegraph at 43rd), as the review says; candidate said Koreatown Northgate.

name: Sam's Log Cabin
kind: Breakfast cafe in a 1930 kit log cabin
why: Breakfast inside a 1930 Sears catalog log cabin that was once a speakeasy and a betting parlor. House-baked scones and a covered garden patio.
story: The cabin went up in 1930 from a Sears Roebuck kit and has been a speakeasy, a roadhouse and an off-track betting room wired to Golden Gate Fields. A breakfast cafe took over in the 1990s, named for the then-owner's son. Kitchen staples are made in house: scones, biscuits, corn bread and cured meats.
order: A scramble with a house-baked scone.
practical: Tue to Sun, 8 am to 2 pm
hours: Tue to Sun 8 am to 2 pm (own site)
flags: Founder Scott Shumaker and the current owners (Rhasaan Fernandez, Mike Daillak) come from a Berkeleyside search summary (not fetchable); names left out.

name: Smokehouse
why: A 1951 burger shack whose grill flares up every minute or so, open late for students, families and neighbors. Cheap, simple and smoky.
story: On the corner of Telegraph and Woolsey since 1951, under a big red sign, with picnic tables and string lights out back. The cooks grill burgers and hot dogs over open flame, and every minute or so the whole grill flares up. Thick fries, crisp onion rings and a chocolate shake round it out, until midnight on weekends.
order: Cheeseburger with grilled onions and a chocolate shake; add chili fries if sharing.
practical: Open until midnight Fri and Sat
hours: Mon to Thu 10:30 am to 11 pm; Fri and Sat to midnight; Sun to 10 pm (KQED, Jan 2026)
flags: Ownership history not found in fetched sources; listing sites say family-owned, left out.
Area set to South Berkeley (Telegraph at Woolsey); candidate said Southside.
Own site not fetched.
